items.stem: A budget owner compares two models. Model X has a lower price per token. Model Y finishes each task with fewer requests. The owner must choose on the cost of one completed task. Which measure meets the constraint?
options: Sum the token prices across all requests for one completed task, then compare the totals.
Compare the per-token list prices, since they are published and stable.
Build a per-developer cost dashboard with attribution before any comparison.
Read the price field in each Messages API response to compare the two models.
items.rationale: A lower token price does not show what a finished task costs. Compare models on cost per completed task, because you pay for completed tasks.
items.trap: The lower per-token price looks cheaper, but the model that needs more requests can cost more per completed task.

items.stem: A proposal moves a quality-sensitive task to a cheaper model tier. The team has no test on its own tasks. The decision must rest on measured quality and cost for real traffic. Which step meets the constraint?
options: Switch the task to the cheaper tier, since its per-token price is lower.
Read the Usage and Cost API totals and treat them as a quality score for each answer.
Sample production tasks weighted like real traffic, and plot each tier score against its spend.
Rebuild the product on three providers, then run a six-month comparison on real traffic.
items.rationale: Production tasks show how each tier performs on real traffic. A score beside the spend shows whether the cheaper tier meets the bar at a lower cost per task.
items.trap: A switch on the lowest per-token price looks like a saving, but the team then has no evidence that the cheaper tier meets the bar.

items.stem: A finance audience and a security audience review a model option. The vendor claims zero risk and perfect accuracy. The record must give each audience the facts it decides on. Select two entries that meet this constraint.
options: Attach the Usage and Cost API export as proof of zero risk.
State the cost per completed task with the date of the price list.
Show the per-token list price alone as the cost field for each option.
Name the measured accuracy with its evaluation set, and give an uncertainty beside it.
items.rationale: Finance decides on cost per completed task, and list prices drift over time. Security needs a measured figure with its evaluation set and uncertainty, not an absolute claim. (Inference)
items.trap: An attached usage export looks like evidence, but that report measures spend, not risk.
